US CLASS 8 Truck Cycle & RKFORGE co-relation 

North America is ~20% of RKFL revenue, so the Class 8 truck cycle has a meaningful impact on earnings. FY26 North America revenue fell 34.9% to ₹688 Cr from ₹1,056 Cr in FY25 due to the heavy-truck downcycle, rather than any product issue at RKFL.

Recovery has started but is incomplete. Q1 FY27 revenue reached ₹222 Cr, up 11.8% YoY and 6.5% QoQ. However, the annualized pace of ~₹889 Cr is still 15.9% below FY25, suggesting further recovery is possible if the cycle continues improving.

What caused the downturn: Post-pandemic excess trucking capacity, weak freight rates and squeezed fleet profitability led carriers to defer new truck purchases. High equipment, financing, insurance, maintenance and labor costs, along with dealer inventory and uncertainty around tariffs/EPA-2027, further pressured OEM production.

Recovery is now replacement-led. Capacity exited the market faster than freight demand fell, improving carrier profitability and forcing deferred fleet replacement. EPA-2027 planning also provides an incentive to replace older trucks. By July 2026, Class 8 net orders were 22,562, up 71% YoY, with an 8.9-month backlog.

Important timing point: 

Truck orders → OEM build schedules → Tier-1 releases → RKFL orders → production/shipping → customs clearance → revenue recognition. 

Therefore, FTR/ACT order data is a leading indicator, not immediate RKFL revenue. With 30–45 days ocean transit plus production and scheduling delays, RKFL's recovery can lag the headline truck-order recovery by several quarters.

Mahanadi Coalfields மூலமாக சுமார் ₹10,000 கோடி திரட்டத் திட்டம் வைத்திருக்கிறார்கள். அதே சமயம் South Eastern Coalfields மூலமாகவும் கிட்டத்தட்ட ₹8,000 முதல் ₹10,000 கோடி வரை எதிர்பார்க்கிறார்கள். இரண்டுமே மிகப்பெரிய நிறுவனங்கள் என்பதில் சந்தேகமே இல்லை. ஆனால், இதில் Coal India கையில் இருக்கிற 25% stake-ஐ விற்கும் Offer For Sale தான் பிரதானமாக இருக்கிறது. South Eastern Coalfields-இல் மட்டும் கூடுதலாக ஒரு 10% fresh shares வெளியிடப் போகிறார்கள்.

ஏற்கனவே Bharat Coking Coal மற்றும் CMPDI லிஸ்ட் ஆனபோது நல்ல லாபம் கொடுத்திருக்கின்றன. Bharat Coking Coal அதன் issue price ₹23-ல் இருந்து 50% உயர்ந்து ₹33.81-ல் வர்த்தகம் ஆகிறது. CMPDI கூட 35% லாபத்தில் இருக்கிறது. ஆனால், வெறும் 25% பங்குகளை மட்டும் வெளியில் விட்டுவிட்டு, முழு கட்டுப்பாட்டையும் கையில் வைத்துக்கொள்ளும் இந்த PSU மாடல் எப்போதுமே ஒரு குழப்பத்தை உருவாக்குகிறது.

Trying to understand Kaynes Technology

Before getting into capex, FCF and valuation, I think it's important to first understand the business and how Kaynes actually makes money.

Kaynes is primarily an EMS company, designing and manufacturing electronic products for customers across industrial, automotive, railway, defence, consumer and other electronics applications. Over time, the company has also been moving further up the value chain towards ODM/value-added manufacturing, where it participates more deeply in product design and development rather than simply assembling a customer's product.

That distinction is important because the economics can potentially be quite different when you own more of the product know-how and engineering.

The smart-metering business is a good example. Under the GridCrest model, Kaynes is involved in designing the meter, manufacturing it, installing it and then maintaining it under a long-term contract with state electricity boards. So the revenue model has two components - manufacturing revenue upfront and an annuity-like O&M component over the ~8-year contract period.

But there is a catch.

The upfront manufacturing revenue creates receivables, and when the customer is a state electricity board, the collection cycle can be long. 
This is what has created significant working-capital pressure and has become one of the biggest issues investors are now trying to understand.

Interestingly, management has openly acknowledged in q1fy27 call that there is more smart-meter business available, but Kaynes is deliberately choosing not to chase it aggressively because of receivables and working-capital concerns.

That makes me wonder: what is the point of winning B2G revenue if the revenue doesn't convert into cash efficiently?

At the same time, the underlying core business doesn't look weak.

Q1FY27 revenue was ₹946 Cr, with standalone EMS growing 53% YoY. Smart-metering revenue was ₹204 Cr, down 12% YoY, while international revenue was ₹102 Cr, up 327%. The order book remains around ₹9,000 Cr.

So the interesting part of the Kaynes story is that while one part of the business is being deliberately moderated because of cash-conversion concerns, the core EMS business is still growing strongly — and the company is simultaneously investing heavily in the next leg of growth through OSAT and PCB manufacturing.

This is where I think the story becomes much more complicated.

FY26 EBITDA was around ₹578 Cr, but working capital consumed roughly ₹1,023 Cr, while OSAT + PCB + EMS capex was around ₹917 Cr.

So despite generating EBITDA, the company ended up with roughly ₹1,841 Cr of negative FCF.

And now management wants to improve balance-sheet strength and cash generation while doing something that is inherently capital intensive:

 building and ramping OSAT and PCB, maintaining strong growth in the core EMS business, and simultaneously fixing the working-capital problem created by the smart-meter business.

That's definitely not a walk in the park.

This is why, as an investor, I'm less interested in simply asking whether the market has already punished Kaynes for the smart-meter fiasco.

The more important question is what happens from here.

Can the core EMS business continue growing fast enough to support the investment cycle? Can OSAT and PCB move from being capital-consuming projects to meaningful cash-generating businesses? Can working-capital intensity structurally normalise? And ultimately, can EBITDA growth translate into FCF growth?

Then there is the valuation question.

The stock has already seen a significant derating from its earlier valuation levels, partly because of concerns around execution, working capital and corporate governance.

So I'm trying to understand whether the current valuation already captures most of these concerns or whether the market is correctly demanding a much higher margin of safety until management proves that growth, capital allocation and cash conversion can all work together.

No view on the stock as of now. Just trying to understand the story. There are still too many open questions in my mind.

The stock did not suddenly move because of one announcement.

The story developed step-by-step:

✅ Q4 FY26 turnaround → Market notices 🤞

Revenue +42% YoY
PAT turned positive
Base business grew ~36%
Base EBITDA margin reached ~26%

↓

Base business proves its quality → Market changes its view

Solara’s base API business is generating ~23–25% EBITDA margins.

But ibuprofen is very different:

₹100 base-business revenue → ~₹24 EBITDA

₹100 ibuprofen revenue → ~₹12 EBITDA loss

So investors started seeing two businesses inside Solara:

Base API business = Good, high-margin earnings engine

Ibuprofen = Structural drag

↓

Why is the base business special?

👉🏻 75%+ of the base business comes from regulated markets.

These markets have strict quality and regulatory requirements. Customers also take time to qualify suppliers, creating barriers to entry and making relationships stickier.

👉🏻 Solara has a differentiated niche in specialised polymer APIs.

These are more complex products and are not simply commodity chemicals. Solara has a strong position in certain polymer markets, giving it a degree of competitive advantage.

👉🏻 The business is diversified across 60+ APIs.

This reduces dependence on one single molecule and gives the company multiple avenues for growth.

👉🏻 Existing manufacturing capacity is only around ~70% utilised.

This means Solara can potentially grow revenue by increasing utilisation and improving product mix before making massive fresh capex.

👉🏻 New DMFs create a future product pipeline.

Management is targeting roughly 4–5 new DMF filings per year. These can become commercial products over the next 2–3 years.

👉🏻 CRAMS provides another long-term option.

It is still small today, but if it scales, it could add a higher-value, higher-margin business.

↓

Ibuprofen strategic review → Potential removal of the structural drag

Management appointed bankers to evaluate strategic options for ibuprofen.

Possible outcome:

Sale / restructuring / repurposing

The important point:

Solara does not necessarily need ibuprofen to become profitable.

Simply removing the loss-making business could improve overall earnings and capital efficiency.

📌 Base EBITDA margin ~23.5%

↓

August breakout + huge volume → Momentum enters

✅ Stronger base business
✅ High margins
✅ Regulated-market exposure
✅ Polymer niche
✅ Potential ibuprofen resolution
✅ Debt reduction
✅ New API pipeline
✅ CRAMS optionality

So the real Solara story is:

Turnaround → Confirmation → Better business mix → Deleveraging → Rerating

The market is increasingly valuing Solara for what it is becoming, not what it was.

A temporary rebound ❓

The reported 26% growth is good.

Manappuram's tonnage rose 7% sequentially to 67 tonnes. FedFina's rose 1%, and its LTV on AUM moved from 61% to 68% because the collateral repriced down. Similar headline percentages to last year, different engine underneath.

YIELDS ARE THE REAL STORY

Muthoot's gold loan yield came in at 17.93%, against 19.56% in Q4 FY26 and 20.76% the quarter before. Management called last year's level a windfall from recoveries and renewals, and now guides 18% to 18.5%. Manappuram went the other way, up around 60 bps to 17.7% on corrective pricing, guiding to the same zone. Two of the largest players converging on one yield while both plan hundreds of new branches is what competition looks like before it reaches the P&L.

READ MUTHOOT STANDALONE

Consolidated PAT grew 43%. Standalone grew 25%. The gap is subsidiaries: Belstar swung from a loss to Rs 66 cr, Muthoot Money's PAT rose 366%. Consolidated PAT was also down 17% sequentially. The gold business is compounding, just not at 43%.

THE NEW RBI RULES

From 1 April, LTV on bullet loans is computed on principal plus interest at maturity. Lenders shifted to periodic interest structures, so a single missed interest payment now flags the whole loan overdue. FedFina's Stage 2 moved from 2.2% to 2.7% on this alone, and Muthoot said the same of its Stage 1 and 2. Both managements call it optical. Fair for now, and worth checking again in two quarters rather than taking on trust.

ONE MORE

IIFL's gold book at Rs 58,406 cr is now larger than Manappuram's Rs 57,006 cr. Though roughly 35% of IIFL's total AUM sits off balance sheet, through co-lending and assignment together, so scale and capital at risk are not the same number.

THE CATCH

Muthoot guides 15% AUM growth for FY27 after delivering 49% in FY26, and declined to guide on profit. Manappuram and FedFina both guide 25% to 30% on gold. The largest lender in the sector and its two challengers are describing the same product in the same year very differently. CSB called Q1 its worst NIM quarter of the year at 3.66%. The FY26 earnings base is being described by the people who produced it as not repeatable.

FY26 was a price story, and AUM growth was the right single metric. FY27 needs tonnage, yield and credit cost sitting next to it.

भारत पूरी तरह से SWIFT के एक 'समानांतर विकल्प'  पर काम कर रहा है, लेकिन भारत का दृष्टिकोण रूस या चीन जैसा आक्रामक नहीं है।

1. वैश्विक स्तर पर: 'BRICS Pay' और CBDC लिंकिंग फ्रेमवर्क भारत BRICS समूह के साथ मिलकर एक नए क्रॉस-बॉर्डर पेमेंट इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर पर चर्चा कर रहा है, जो पश्चिमी देशों के प्रभुत्व वाले SWIFT नेटवर्क पर निर्भरता को कम करेगा:

घरेलू सिस्टम को जोड़ना: इस योजना के तहत भारत के UPI, ब्राजील के Pix, चीन के CIPS और रूस के SPFS को एक साझा नेटवर्क से जोड़ा जा रहा है ताकि बिना SWIFT मैसेजिंग के सीधे वित्तीय लेनदेन हो सके।

डिजिटल करेंसी (CBDC) नेटवर्क: हाल ही में RBI गवर्नर संजय मल्होत्रा ने पुष्टि की है कि BRICS देशों की सेंट्रल बैंक डिजिटल करेंसी (CBDCs) को आपस में जोड़ने के विकल्प पर गंभीरता से विचार किया जा रहा है। भारत इस प्रस्ताव को BRICS समिट 2026 के मुख्य एजेंडे में शामिल कर रहा है।

2. घरेलू स्तर पर: भारत का अपना 'SFMS' सिस्टम

बहुत कम लोग जानते हैं कि भारत के पास पहले से ही SWIFT जैसा अपना एक सुरक्षित मैसेजिंग सिस्टम है:इसे SFMS  कहा जाता है।वर्तमान में भारत के भीतर सभी बैंकों के बीच होने वाले बड़े लेनदेन (जैसे RTGS और NEFT) इसी SFMS के ज़रिए होते हैं।भारत अब इस SFMS सिस्टम को अंतरराष्ट्रीय स्तर पर अन्य देशों के केंद्रीय बैंकों के साथ जोड़ने की संभावनाएं तलाश रहा है।

भारत की इस रणनीति में एक महत्वपूर्ण कूटनीतिक संतुलन है जिसे समझना ज़रूरी है:

रूस और चीन का रुख (आक्रामक): रूस (प्रतिबंधों के कारण) और चीन राजनीतिक कारणों से SWIFT का ऐसा विकल्प चाहते हैं जो पश्चिमी वित्तीय प्रणाली को पूरी तरह से बायपास कर सके।

भारत का रुख (व्यावहारिक): भारत अमेरिका या पश्चिमी देशों से संबंध खराब नहीं करना चाहता। भारत के वाणिज्य मंत्री पीयूष गोयल और विदेश मंत्री एस. जयशंकर ने स्पष्ट किया है कि भारत किसी 'साझा ब्रिक्स मुद्रा'  के पक्ष में नहीं है। भारत का मुख्य उद्देश्य केवल अपने व्यापारियों के लिए लेनदेन की लागत  को कम करना, अपने UPI का वैश्विक विस्तार करना और देश की वित्तीय संप्रभुता को सुरक्षित रखना है।
भारत किसी राजनीतिक विरोध के कारण नहीं, बल्कि आर्थिक समझदारी, कम लागत और डिजिटल तकनीक (UPI/CBDC) के दम पर वैश्विक वित्तीय बाजार में SWIFT के एकाधिकार को चुनौती दे रहा है।
अमेरिका और पश्चिमी देशों को भली-भांति पता है कि रूस पर लगे प्रतिबंधों के बाद भारत लगातार अन्य देशों (जैसे UAE, रूस, मॉरीशस) के साथ अपनी स्थानीय मुद्रा (रुपये) में व्यापार बढ़ा रहा है।यदि भारत पूरी तरह से SWIFT को बायपास कर देता है, तो अमेरिकी डॉलर का दबदबा कमजोर हो जाएगा।इसलिए, पश्चिमी देश और वित्तीय संस्थाएं भारत को SWIFT के भीतर ही अधिक महत्व, नई सुविधाएं और मजबूत स्थिति देना चाहती हैं, ताकि भारत इस मुख्यधारा के वैश्विक वित्तीय तंत्र का हिस्सा बना रहे।

हाल ही में SWIFT ने भारत के UPI की ताकत को देखते हुए भारतीय बैंकों (जैसे SBI, HDFC, ICICI और Axis Bank) के साथ मिलकर एक नया रिटेल क्रॉस-बॉर्डर पेमेंट्स फ्रेमवर्क लॉन्च किया है। भारत का UPI वर्तमान में दुनिया के लगभग आधे रियल-टाइम डिजिटल ट्रांजैक्शन को संभालता है। SWIFT को पता है कि अगर उसने भारत को अपने साथ प्रमुखता से नहीं जोड़ा, तो भारत का UPI और 'BRICS Pay' मिलकर SWIFT के वैश्विक एकाधिकार को खत्म कर देंगे।
